_comment: The C³ Arcade reads this at runtime (tools/arcade/index.html) and the Break Room's rail chip counts it for its 'N GAMES' label (assets/cinema.js, the `marquee` field in data/tools.json). ADDING A GAME IS THIS FILE AND data/tools.json — nothing else. No code change, no fingerprint run, no build step, and NO ARTWORK: the arcade keys each game's menu row, preview screen and screen glow from `tint` and `title` (v27: one photographed cabinet, arcade/room/), which is what keeps 'one row' true. Every game needs a row HERE (so the arcade lists it) and a row in data/tools.json with the same `slug` (so #/tool/<slug> opens it, the phone list finds it by search and the C³ menu lists it); the arcade never prints or links to a game's real URL — every row links to `#/tool/<slug>`, and the game it loads INTO the cabinet screen is resolved from the same data/tools.json row the site's viewer uses, never from this file — because reps must never see a repository hostname — see claude/v15-framed-data-and-hidden-repos.md.

_schema.slug: REQUIRED. The tool slug. Must match a `slug` in data/tools.json exactly — that row is what the launch link (#/tool/<slug>) resolves against, and a game whose slug is not in tools.json is listed with its launch disabled and a plain note saying so.
_schema.title: REQUIRED. The name on the marquee, as the game itself spells it. The arcade prints THIS, never the tool's label, so a game whose page carries no <title> (After Hours does not) still reads correctly. Keep it short and uppercase — it is fitted to the marquee and to a 320px attract screen, and a very long one wraps to two lines rather than shrinking to mush.
_schema.blurb: REQUIRED. One line — what the game is, in the room's voice. It is the subtitle on the cabinet's attract screen and the HOW TO PLAY copy, wrapped to two and three lines respectively, so write it to read well cut short.
_schema.url: The game's real address. RECORDED, NOT RENDERED: the arcade never prints it and never links to it. data/tools.json is what the viewer actually loads; this is here so the manifest is a complete record of the cabinet and so a mismatch between the two files is visible in a diff.
_schema.tint: OPTIONAL. A hex from theme.css §02 that keys this cabinet ALONE: its T-molding, the marquee's underline and border, its side art, the bloom behind its screen, and the palette its attract loop draws in. It never touches PRESS START, the room, or any body text, so no tint can break contrast or make the call to action unrecognisable. Defaults to --brass #c8973f. Use a token value, never a new colour.
